assessment.nobel_worthiness: Opening a new observational window with a cubic-kilometre detector in Antarctic ice is the kind of instrument-led discovery I weigh most heavily. The 2013 detection of a diffuse astrophysical neutrino flux, followed by the 2017 TXS 0506+056 association and the Galactic-plane neutrino map, makes neutrino astronomy a real field. It also ties directly to the cosmic-ray origin problem.
assessment.attribution: Halzen drove the IceCube concept and the science case, and Spiering was a long-time spokesperson and leader of the neutrino-telescope programme from Baikal and AMANDA onward. Two laureates is a tidy configuration, but a large collaboration built it and the credit is not clean. The supplied credit omits other pioneers (for example the DUMAND and AMANDA lineage) and I cannot independently verify the relative contributions.
assessment.maturity: Detection of the diffuse flux is well established and has been confirmed independently through different channels. Source identification is still limited to a few objects, so the field is young but the discovery itself is solid and the recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should cover the diffuse-flux discovery or wait for firmer source identification
Credit among Halzen, Spiering and the wider collaboration or earlier pioneers is not fully resolved
I have not independently verified individual leadership roles

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks reach fractional uncertainty near 1e-18, which is a real step in precision measurement. The magic-wavelength lattice idea resolves the trapping-shift problem. The clocks are used for tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and Ye built the leading demonstrations at JILA. The pair is a clean two-person attribution. The frequency-comb and ion-clock lineage was partly recognized in 2005 and 2012, so the allocation against that earlier work needs care.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups have confirmed the performance, and the field is mature. Recognition looks timely, though the redefinition of the second is not yet done.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier prizes for combs and single-ion control
Atomic clocks are outside my own expertise, so I would lean on colleagues and expert reviewers
Comparison to ion clocks and other lattice groups for credit

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imaging the shadow of M87* in 2019 and Sgr A* in 2022 required a global VLBI array at 1.3 mm, with serious calibration and imaging methods. This is a landmark instrument achievement with direct bearing on black-hole physics, in line with the 2020 prize recognition of black holes.
assessment.attribution: Doeleman led the EHT effort, Falcke proposed the shadow-imaging idea and Moran led the mm-VLBI technique development. A three-person configuration is possible but defensible only with a large collaboration behind the images. Credit among many instrument and imaging leaders is contested.
assessment.maturity: Two independent targets and multiple imaging pipelines support the results, and the polarization images add to them. The interpretation of the ring is stable, though precision tests of gravity are still limited. Recognition is plausible but could also be seen as early.
uncertainties: Collaboration size makes individual credit hard
The exact role split between Falcke, Moran and Doeleman is unverified by me
Whether physics results beyond imaging are mature enough

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the 2018 observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity opened the field of moire quantum materials. It has spawned a very large body of work and a new tunable platform for correlated physics.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 prediction and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 experiments. This is a natural theory plus experiment split, though the experiment is often shared with Cory Dean's group and other collaborators and the supplied names exclude some of them.
assessment.maturity: Replicated widely across many labs, with fractional Chern insulators and related phenomena, though the microscopic origin of the superconductivity is unsettled. Recognition is timely but the field is still moving quickly.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is unresolved
Condensed matter is outside my own field, so my judgment is secondhand
Possible omissions from the credited set

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Realizing the superfluid to Mott insulator transition and then Fermi-Hubbard physics and quantum-gas microscopes turned ultracold atoms into a programmable quantum simulator. It is a broad, lasting scientific impact on many-body physics.
assessment.attribution: The experimental trio of Greiner, Bloch and Esslinger forms a natural group with clear contributions. Cirac and Zoller proposed the Bose-Hubbard idea and the theory, and their contribution is real but the five credited names cannot all be honoured. I choose the experimental three, with the knowledge that the theory side deserves recognition elsewhere.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many groups for two decades, but the application to open problems beyond classical computability is still being demonstrated. Reasonably mature.
uncertainties: Fair division between theory proposals and experimental realization
Overlap with Nobel recognition for cold atoms in 1997 and 2001
This is outside my own expertise

assessment.nobel_worthiness: SASE free-electron lasers deliver coherent, femtosecond X-ray pulses at LCLS, European XFEL and elsewhere. They have enabled new science in structural biology, ultrafast chemistry and materials. As an instrument, the impact is large and a clear step in photon sources.
assessment.attribution: Pellegrini and Kim developed the SASE theory and the high-gain concept, and Rossbach led the FLASH and European XFEL development. The credit is broadly clean for these three, but the accelerator community also credits others such as Bonifacio and the LCLS team and I cannot settle that on my own.
assessment.maturity: Well established, with several operating machines worldwide. The discovery is mature and recognition would be timely in terms of impact, though it is arguably a technology prize.
uncertainties: Whether the Nobel committee views this as physics or engineering
Missing credit for early SASE theorists such as Bonifacio
I have not checked individual contribution dates

assessment.nobel_worthiness: GW170817 and AT2017gfo, with kilonova theory predicting r-process heating, confirmed neutron-star mergers as a heavy-element site. This is a clean multimessenger result that links nuclear and astrophysics.
assessment.attribution: Metzger and Kasen developed the kilonova models, and Tanvir led the observational discovery of a kilonova in a short GRB (2013) alongside others. Lattimer and Schramm made the earlier prediction of decompression of neutron-star matter, which complicates credit. The detection itself is a collaboration achievement already partly recognized with the 2017 LIGO prize.
assessment.maturity: The observation is a single well-studied event with a few other candidates, so the population picture is incomplete. The r-process yield per merger is still debated, so the maturity is moderate.
uncertainties: Only one confirmed event
Relative credit among Lattimer, Metzger, Kasen and observers
Overlap with 2017 gravitational-wave prize

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The LHC and its general-purpose detectors, ATLAS and CMS, enabled the Higgs boson discovery and the large precision programme of the Standard Model. As a detector builder I value the instrument achievement and the decades of patient engineering behind it.
assessment.attribution: Evans led the LHC machine, and Della Negra and Jenni conceived and led CMS and ATLAS respectively. A configuration of three is possible but would downplay thousands of colleagues, and the physics discovery was already honoured in 2013 for theory. I am not sure the committee would credit construction without a new physics result.
assessment.maturity: The machine and detectors are fully mature and confirmed by operation. The question is only whether a prize for construction is timely or appropriate now.
uncertainties: Whether the Statutes' discovery or invention criterion is met by a facility
Overlap with the 2013 Higgs prize
Choice among many instrument leaders is difficult
